# PGmc disagreement map

GENERATED analytical view; source forms remain separately authoritative.
Reading coverage, analytical review and explanatory certainty are independent.

Core triage compares the recorded citation units and retains every core alternative.
Tags identify reviewed questions; undetermined cases are not settled historical disagreements.
Unknown attribution or date is a review outcome, not source endorsement or a PGmc default.

Citation-unit triage, feature alignment and explanations of divergence have separate accountability.
Position-support reasons do not certify an explanation of inter-author disagreement.

Core cases: 393; different_units: 30; insufficient_evidence: 47; substantive_difference: 2; undetermined: 314.
Core alignment: bounded_limit: 73; unreviewed: 320.
The catalogue below covers every case. Detailed explanations follow only where reasoning is recorded;
the linked source ledger retains the complete alternatives, arguments and verification limits.

Fulk independently supplies a PGmc citation but its OE back mutation does not establish PGmc e-to-i raising. See beaver-colour-direction for the separately bounded analytical argument.

- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Fulk69's explicit earlier PGmc *bebruz is an example for OE e > eo back mutation, conditioned by following a or u/o. [Fulk2018 pp.69; Fulk2018 pp.69; Fulk2018 pp.69]
  Premises: The process is explicitly OE; the following-u tag is not a claim of PGmc u-raising. Counterarguments/limits: This does not explain the bebr/bebur formation difference, reversed semantic derivation or selected befer spelling.

Written present-root e/i differs between endorsed dictionary citations; Kroonen's rejected i is not agreement and Orel's long-i antecedent is another formation. Ringe explicitly supports short-i through following-j raising. Fulk supplies a j-present argument, not an authored PGmc word; Ringe-Taylor distinguishes underlying/surface and later finite cells with native-text limits. These feature/unit/attribution distinctions are reviewed, but common-endpoint equivalence and the inter-author cause remain unestablished.

- position_support / sound_law (source_explicit): Ringe pp.151-152 supply short-e ask intermediates before short-i PGmc present forms, and p.273 explicitly attributes the raised present-root vowel to j. [Ringe2017 pp.151-152,273; Ringe2017 pp.128]
  Premises: The source's ask etymon and short-vowel present derivation are distinguished from offer and from long-ī wait. This records a position argument under Ringe's stated conditioner; it does not back-date the intermediates or manufacture a PGmc e-bearing infinitive. Counterarguments/limits: Kroonen's defended e-bearing stem and Orel's long-i antecedent require their own representational and derivational premises. This does not establish why the authors disagree or complete the conditioning census.

Those allow a premised bridge, not established identity of Orel's specific bind representation. [Orel2003 pp.xii; Ringe2017 pp.252; Orel2003 pp.41; Kroonen2013 pp.64]
  Premises: Require evidence that Orel's bind e has the appropriate underlying/derivational status; his phonemic-opposition stance remains a separate issue. Counterarguments/limits: The method alone does not explain this headword or date it; no global dictionary e/i normalization.

  Premises: The secondary zero grade is remodelled; it is not Orel's secondary a-grade or selected board cell. Counterarguments/limits: Orel's reason for omitting z is not thereby established.

The borrowing-direction opposition is real; its explanatory relation is analyst inference, not an author-vote verdict or known reason for Orel's rejection of the gemination account.

  Premises: Ringe's general objection is not Orel's stated causal explanation. Counterarguments/limits: Test original n-paradigm and chronology independently; no law or selected input is changed.

Kroonen278, Ringe310 and RT205,231 reconstruct a neuter s/z-stem singular kalbaz; Fulk176-178 and RT385-386 retain distinct genitive/plural calfur and unresolved histories. Orel209's m./n. citation is not class proof.

- position_support / pie_reconstruction (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: Old s-stem with explicitly different singular/plural vowels; rejects Greek womb comparison on initial labiovelar and root-vowel grounds. [Kroonen2013 pp.278]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / pie_reconstruction (source_explicit): Recorded argument for this position: OE cealf is explicitly cited. Despite the initial-consonant discrepancy, Orel relates the word to Sanskrit garbha 'womb' and associated Indo-European formations; the bibliography also records an older s-stem proposal. [Orel2003 pp.209]
  Premises: The reason applies only to the stated unit/position; it does not select CAPR's current input. Counterarguments/limits: This is the position's own stated argument, not an established explanation of the difference between authors. Alternatives, cells and historical stages still require alignment; inherited bibliography proposals are not automatically endorsed.
- position_support / morphological_argument (source_explicit): Kroonen278, Ringe310-311 and RT205,231 explicitly allow neuter z-stem singular kalbaz alongside oblique/plural kalbiz forms; az alone does not identify masculine a-stem. [Kroonen2013 pp.278; Kroonen2013 pp.278; Ringe2017 pp.310; Ringe2017 pp.310; RingeTaylor2014 pp.205]
  Premises: Selected singular, oblique stem and plural are different units. Counterarguments/limits: The original Anglian paradigm is not thereby explained.
- position_support / analogy (source_explicit): Fulk176-178 calls the rhotacism/syncope/parasiting explanation likeliest but challenges it; RT385-386 doubts iz/uz and levelling scenarios and cannot specify a father-analogy mechanism. Identical calfur genitive and plural are not one cell. [Fulk2018 pp.176-178; Fulk2018 pp.177; Fulk2018 pp.178; RingeTaylor2014 pp.386; RingeTaylor2014 pp.385; RingeTaylor2014 pp.385]
  Premises: Actual cell receipts constrain hypotheses; reported analogy is not adopted CAPR grammar. Counterarguments/limits: Further original-paradigm evidence is missing.

Ringe268 limits laryngeal pedigree to chew. [Orel2003 pp.213; Kroonen2013 pp.286-287; Ringe2017 pp.268; Ringe2017 pp.268]
  Premises: Optional w in a past cell is not added j in the present or a reopened released glide law. Counterarguments/limits: The relationship between the particular kj/jj proposal and rejected required j remains a named premise, not complete equivalence.

[RingeTaylor2014 pp.115; RingeTaylor2014 pp.520; RingeTaylor2014 pp.520; RingeTaylor2014 pp.520; RingeTaylor2014 pp.520; Fulk2018 pp.162,253]

[Fulk2018 pp.12; Fulk2018 pp.81; Fulk2018 pp.73; Fulk2018 pp.81; RingeTaylor2014 pp.174; Ringe2017 pp.315]

[RingeTaylor2014 pp.211; RingeTaylor2014 pp.211; RingeTaylor2014 pp.347; RingeTaylor2014 pp.350; RingeTaylor2014 pp.350; RingeTaylor2014 pp.350]
  Premises: Read the complete cited argument; source qualification, cell and stage are independent. Selected j-verb is not stative ā, secure-fastening inon, fasting abstract or adjective; formation and root-compound admissibility remain separate.
